user: And what are the typical timelines?
answer:
What I did: I opened the dispute for service_not_rendered and escalated it to a human agent.

What I found in our process guidelines:
- Card disputes: review target is 10 business days.
- Transfer disputes: review target is 20 business days.
- Complex cases (for example involving a foreign acquirer) can run to 45 calendar days; you will be notified if your case moves into that category.
- Provisional credit is applied within 2 business days only where the reason code is a fraud code and the disputed amount exceeds EUR 50; it can be reversed if the dispute is declined.

What happens next: a human agent will follow up by the account email and may request supporting documents. You may withdraw the dispute before resolution if you choose. If you’d like, I can send a statement for the account period you need to the email registered on your account — shall I send one?

fragments.text:
Dispute handling process
## Provisional credit
Where the disputed amount exceeds EUR 50 and the reason code is a fraud code, a
provisional credit is applied within two business days. Provisional credit is
reversed if the dispute is later declined.

Glossary
## Provisional credit
A temporary refund applied while a dispute is reviewed; reversed if the dispute
is declined.

Dispute handling process
## Review timelines
The review target is 10 business days for card reason codes and 20 business
days for transfer reason codes. Complex cases involving a foreign acquirer may
run to 45 calendar days; the customer is notified when that happens.

Verta tariff schedule
## Transfer fees by type
| Transfer type | Flat fee | Percentage fee |
|---|---|---|
| Internal | EUR 0.00 | 0% |
| SEPA | EUR 0.35 | 0% |
| SWIFT | EUR 15.00 | 0.3% |
| Card payment | EUR 0.00 | 1.2% |

The percentage fee is calculated on the EUR equivalent of the transfer amount.
